items.title: Benny Golson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I think it was Terence Blanchard and Donald Harrison. They were in the group then.

ctx.x: According to this chronology, you were with Art Blakey again in ’83 and then again in ’89. He passed in ’90. What was it like coming back, working with Art Blakey? He still had that same fire, that same magic?

Coming back to a drummer swinging like that was like paradise. It’s like going to get another gourmet meal. That was – when I came back, it was as the All-Star Jazz Messengers: his current group, plus Jackie McLean, Curtis, and me. That’s what that was, those tours. It wasn’t just the regular group. The last time we did it, I think it was Terence Blanchard and Donald Harrison. They were in the group then.

By this time, coming back to New York, shortly thereafter, is the arrival of the Marsalis brothers with Bu. Do you recall what kind of impact that was having in changing the course of jazz? Or did it? Was it even ostensible at that time?
